tools.name: ks_find_target
tools.description: Find the company or Knowledge Studio layer a person means. Returns candidates: each company with its type (a company, or a person's own individual record), owner email and the layer it runs, and given a login email, the record that account works in (login_company_of); each layer with its kind, whether it holds unpublished changes, who saved its draft since it was last published (draft_saves), the companies bound to it directly, the companies reached through layers below it (with the version their running package reads), and every layer a publish has to go through with its own draft_saves. Selects a target only when exactly one matched and it is safe to.

query.description: A company name or id, the email an account signs in with, a layer name or stable_id, or a Console link.
query.title: Query

tools.name: ks_read_layer
tools.description: Read one layer of any kind by part: overview (baseline to copy into a patch, vocabulary, owned counts, unpublished changes and who saved them, a ready patch_frame), objects (catalog of owned and inherited records, filter by kind or search, paged; payload adds each filtered row's whole record), settings (Delegated Settings it may answer, search by stable_id or label), schema (one kind's JSON Schema and example), guide (one section of the agent guide), release_plan (read-only list of layers to publish, in order, to reach target_organization_ids, with every record each layer ships as that release builds it and who saved its draft, a plan_checksum the Console shows as its Plan id, and release_organization_ids to hand on).

kind.description: objects: filter by kind. schema: the kind whose schema to return.
kind.title: Kind

search.description: objects / settings: match stable_id or name.
search.title: Search

payload.description: objects, with a kind or a search: each row also carries its whole record, as ks_read_object returns it.
payload.title: Payload

section.description: guide: a section number or a word of its title. Omit to list sections.
section.title: Section

target_organization_ids.description: release_plan: the companies to bring up, as ids. Omit to list who could be chosen.
target_organization_ids.title: Target Organization Ids

tools.name: ks_read_object
tools.description: Read every record the layer owns or inherits under one kind and stable_id, each with its owner. Several layers may hold one (overrides reuse the stable_id of what they override); all are returned. records reads up to 25 identities in one call. Edit a record by starting from what this returns, never from memory.

kind.description: An object kind, or delegated_setting / layer_setting.
kind.title: Kind

stable_id.description: For layer_setting, the entry_stable_id it answers.
stable_id.title: Stable Id

kind.description: An object kind, or delegated_setting / layer_setting.
kind.title: Kind

stable_id.description: For layer_setting, the entry_stable_id it answers.
stable_id.title: Stable Id

records.description: Read several records in one call instead of kind and stable_id: each answer is shaped as a single read is, in the order asked.
records.title: Records

tools.name: ks_preview
tools.description: Preview an Interchange patch against the layer: what it would add, change and remove, every issue, whether it is applicable and publishable, and the two checksums an apply must send back. An applicable preview is kept for 24 hours (kept_for_apply), so ks_apply can send just the checksums. When someone else has saved unpublished changes to the layer, others_saving names them with a warning: those publish with this change. Writes nothing to the layer.

tools.name: ks_apply
tools.description: Apply a previewed patch to the layer's draft (never publishes). Send the preview's context_checksum and diff_checksum, and leave the document out to apply the one that preview kept; send it again only when the preview was not kept or has expired (preview_not_kept). A change this layer has already applied returns its receipt (already_applied) instead of writing again. Only after the person asked to save a draft.

document.description: Omit to apply the document an applicable ks_preview of this layer returned these checksums for in the last 24 hours.
document.title: Document

reapply_of.description: Only to re-apply a change that was applied and then undone, after the person confirmed: the apply_id of that change's latest apply.
reapply_of.title: Reapply Of

tools.name: ks_replay
tools.description: Queue Replay: run every saved real order the layer reaches against the current drafts, or, with release_organization_ids, the orders of the companies a release moves against the stack that release leaves in force. wait_seconds waits for the runs and answers with their status. Read progress and differences with ks_replay_results.

release_organization_ids.description: The release plan's release_organization_ids, copied as they are: runs only the cases of the companies that release moves, each against the stack the release leaves in force. Release layers are read as drafts; every other layer as the release leaves it -- a release layer's direct dependencies at their active version, and above those through the versions their packages pin, not every layer at its active version. Omit to run against every layer's current draft.
release_organization_ids.title: Release Organization Ids

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds (at most 15) for the runs, and answer with their status as ks_replay_results action=status would.
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds

tools.name: ks_replay_results
tools.description: Read Replay results: action=status reports each case by company (with what can and cannot be said about the drafts a run read; pass release_organization_ids to read a release's runs, and wait_seconds to wait for runs still going), case_inputs returns one saved case's job (context, answers, instances) in the shape ks_resolve takes, case_diff shows one case's component, SKU and form differences, paged (components that changed the same way are one row listing their instance_ids; candidates as SKU codes; a tier the same on both sides is named in same_on_both_sides; missing_facts says what a Slot waiting on inputs needs; form lists Questions whose wording, visibility, required flag, options or default moved, and readiness and warning changes, with form_compared false when the baseline predates the form check).

release_organization_ids.description: The same ids ks_replay was given, to read that release's runs.
release_organization_ids.title: Release Organization Ids

wait_seconds.description: With action=status: wait up to this many seconds (at most 15; more is cut to 15) for queued and running cases to finish before answering.
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds

tools.name: ks_resolve
tools.description: Resolve one job for a company and read what it comes to, without saving anything: the same run a Replay case of it makes, over the whole Enterprise library ranked as the engine ranks it (no branch shelf, no stock order -- compare with the prototype on All branches). Returns the by-SKU totals (demand and order quantity with units), each instance's components (status, quantity, the SKU and name it defaults to, missing_facts while pending), Rule warnings and unanswered required Questions; instances that came out the same are one entry listing their instance_ids. Copy a real job from ks_replay_results action=case_inputs. With previewed, it reads a change an applicable ks_preview kept as if it were applied, writing nothing: try a change on a job before saving it. Takes as long as a resolve in the prototype, often 20 seconds or more.

instance_id.description: Your own name for it, such as gate-1, repeated in the result.
instance_id.title: Instance Id

inputs.description: What this one thing states for itself, by Fact or Attribute stable_id: a run's length, a gate's opening and type, an answer it gives differently from the job.
inputs.title: Inputs

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

trade.description: The Trade layer's stable_id, such as fence.
trade.title: Trade

context.description: What selects the questionnaire, keyed by full stable_id, such as fence.attribute.material_system.
context.title: Context

answers.description: The job's answers, keyed by the Attribute's full stable_id (fence.attribute.segment, not segment).
answers.title: Answers

instances.description: One entry per thing on the drawing: seven end posts are seven entries. There is no count.
instances.title: Instances

layers.description: drafts reads every layer of the company's stack as its current draft, other people's unpublished changes included.
layers.title: Layers

effective_on.description: The day the job is priced for. Omit for today.
effective_on.title: Effective On

previewed.description: With layers: drafts, read this layer as an applicable ks_preview of the last 24 hours would leave it -- its layer_stable_id and the two checksums that preview returned -- without applying it.

tools.name: ks_applies
tools.description: The layer's 20 most recent applies (who, when, counts, and whether each can still be undone: undo.state current, rebasable, conflicts with the records in the way, or not_kept), or one apply's undo: undo_document is the document to preview and apply, rebased onto the layer as it stands when only records the apply did not touch have moved, and null when it cannot be undone. Use it to confirm whether an apply landed before ever re-sending one.

apply_id.description: Give one to get that apply's undo document.
apply_id.title: Apply Id

tools.name: ks_read_catalog
tools.description: Read a company's Product catalog: whose library it is (a company on its Enterprise's library shares it with every company there), how many Products, how many are tagged with a Role and how many not, counts by Role, and the latest AI tagging runs with progress and outcome, including the rows a run skipped and why. wait_seconds waits for a run still going. search (SKU or name) and/or role list the matching rows, 50 a page, each with its Roles, stated Attributes and selling terms. vocabulary: true adds the Roles and Attributes the catalog is described in, read from the company's own knowledge with its drafts, 15 Roles a page (vocabulary_page; vocabulary_search narrows the Roles): hold a supplier's values against it before importing.

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds (at most 15; more is cut to 15) for a tagging run to finish.
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds

search.description: List catalog rows whose SKU or name contains this, paged.
search.title: Search

role.description: List rows tagged with this Role stable_id, paged.
role.title: Role

vocabulary.description: Also return the vocabulary: every Role the company may tag with, each naming its Attributes, and every Attribute once with its type, unit, allowed values and whether a layer below the Trade may add values (extensible_below). 15 Roles a page, each page with the Attributes its Roles state.
vocabulary.title: Vocabulary

vocabulary_search.description: With vocabulary: only Roles whose stable_id or name contains this, such as a material system (chain_link, vinyl).
vocabulary_search.title: Vocabulary Search

tools.name: ks_catalog_import_preview
tools.description: Preview importing Products into a company's catalog from CSV text (Name; optionally ArcSite ID, SKU, Description). A row finds its Product by ArcSite ID, then SKU, then name; one that finds none adds a Product, and Products the sheet leaves out are left alone. Says how many would be created, updated and unchanged, and every row that cannot be imported. Writes nothing.

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

csv.description: The sheet as CSV text: a header row naming Name and optionally ArcSite ID, SKU and Description, then one row per Product. Other columns are ignored. There is no file argument: read the file yourself and pass its text here.
csv.title: Csv

tools.name: ks_catalog_import_apply
tools.description: Import the same CSV text into the company's catalog: all rows or, if any row is wrong, none. Live at once -- a catalog has no draft. Only after a clean preview and the person asked to import. Roles, Attributes and selling are never touched; tag afterwards with ks_catalog_tag.

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

csv.description: The sheet as CSV text: a header row naming Name and optionally ArcSite ID, SKU and Description, then one row per Product. Other columns are ignored. There is no file argument: read the file yourself and pass its text here.
csv.title: Csv

tools.name: ks_catalog_tag
tools.description: AI tagging of a company's catalog. action=start queues a run that tags only Products with no Role yet, and on those only Attributes they do not state; limit tags only the newest few (after an import, the rows it added) to check. action=undo takes back what one run wrote, except rows a person has changed since. Live at once. Only after the person asked. Read progress with ks_read_catalog.

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

limit.description: start: tag only the newest this many untagged Products -- after an import, the ones it added -- to check the result before the rest. Omit for all of them.
limit.title: Limit

task_id.description: undo: the run to take back, as ks_read_catalog lists it.
task_id.title: Task Id

tools.name: ks_catalog_edit
tools.description: Write a company's catalog directly: a batch of edits, each naming rows by SKU (or product id) and any of a Role tag added or taken off, Attribute values stated or cleared under that Role, and selling terms. Every edit is checked first; one that cannot be made refuses the whole batch and nothing is written. dry_run (the default) reports what would change; dry_run=false writes. Either way the answer gives counts per edit and the changed SKUs; detail=true adds each changed row's before and after, grouped by the change. Live at once in the company's library -- an Enterprise library is shared by every branch -- and there is no undo: correct a mistake with another edit. Only after the person asked.

product_ids.description: For rows with no SKU, as the catalog lists them.
product_ids.title: Product Ids

role.description: The Role stable_id the rows are bought as. Needed for tag and for stating values: the Role decides which Attributes may be stated. Clearing a value (an empty list) needs none.
role.title: Role

tag.description: true tags the rows with role, false takes that tag off, omit to leave tags alone.
tag.title: Tag

attributes.description: Attribute stable_id to the values the rows state, in the vocabulary's words; an empty list takes the statement back. The Role's selection policy is one of these Attributes.
attributes.title: Attributes

preset.description: default: sold in the unit it is demanded in, no unit. unstated: a selling unit nobody has measured. packages: whole packages of amount each. converted: each unit of demand costs amount of the selling unit.
preset.title: Preset

extra.description: A fixed amount of the selling unit added once per job.
extra.title: Extra

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id

dry_run.description: true (the default) reports what would change and writes nothing.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

detail.description: true returns every changed row's before and after; the default returns counts per edit and the changed SKUs.
detail.title: Detail

tools.name: ks_create_layer
tools.description: Create an empty Manufacturer, Enterprise or Organization Overlay standing on one layer, as the Console's New layer dialog does. It starts with an empty 0.0.0 version that reads what its parent reads; nobody runs it until a company is bound to it. Its records are written with ks_preview / ks_apply like any layer's. Only after the person asked.

parent_layer_stable_id.description: The layer it stands on: for a company's own Overlay, the layer the company runs now.
parent_layer_stable_id.title: Parent Layer Stable Id

stable_id.description: Omit to derive it from the name.
stable_id.title: Stable Id

tools.name: ks_bind_company
tools.description: Make a layer the one a company runs, moving it off the layer it ran (returned as previous_layer). Changes that company's quotes at once: on a layer nothing has published, it cannot quote, nor its catalog be AI-tagged, until the layer is published in the Console. Only after the person asked.

organization_id.description: The company's id as ks_find_target lists it, as a string.
organization_id.title: Organization Id
